question.text: If the binding energy of ground state electron in a hydrogen atom is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>13</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>eV</mi></math>, then, the energy required to remove the electron from the second excited state of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Li</mi><msup><mo> </mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> will be: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>eV</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _____.

solution.text:
Given:

Binding energy, EH=E0=13.6 eV.

Now for hydrogen like atom, we can write

ELi2+=E0Z2n2=13.6×99=13.6 eV

=136×10-1 eV

Therefore, x=136.
